statement.p: The motion of a solid object can be analyzed by thinking of the mass as concentrated at a single point, the center of mass. If the object has density \rho(x,y,z) at the point (x,y,z) and occupies a region W, then the coordinates (\overline{x},\overline{y},\overline{z}) of the center of mass are given by \overline{x} = \frac{1}{m}\int_W x\rho \, dV \quad \overline{y} = \frac{1}{m}\int_W y\rho \, dV \quad \overline{z} = \frac{1}{m}\int_W z\rho \, dV,

Assume x, y, z are in cm. Let C be a solid cone with both height and radius 2 and contained between the surfaces z=\sqrt{x^2+y^2} and z=2. If C has constant mass density of 4 g/cm^3, find the z-coordinate of C's center of mass.

static.solution: \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h = \frac{8}{3}\pi, so the total mass is \frac{32}{3} \pi (since the density is always 4). The center of mass z-coordinate is given by \overline{z} = \frac{3}{32 \pi} \int_C z \,dV Using cylindrical coordinates to evaluate this integral gives \overline{z} = \frac{3}{32 \pi} \int_0^{2\pi} \int_0^{2} \int_0^z 4 z r\,dr \,dz \,d\theta, so \overline{z} = \frac{3}{32 \pi} \int_0^{2\pi} \int_0^{2} 4\cdot \frac{z^3}{2} \,dz \,d\theta = \left(\frac{3}{32 \pi}\right)\left(2\pi\right) 4\cdot \frac{16}{8} = \frac{3}{2}\mbox{ cm}.
